title: Rigveda 1.43: To Rudra and Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.43: To Rudra and Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.43 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Rudra and Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 29v-30r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.43.1-2 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 3, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 29v
translation.original_text:
1kad ru̱drāya̱ prace̍tase mī̱ḻhuṣṭa̍māya̱ tavya̍se | vo̱cema̱ śaṁta̍maṁ hṛ̱de ||
2yathā̍ no̱ adi̍ti̱ḥ kara̱t paśve̱ nṛbhyo̱ yathā̱ gave̍ | yathā̍ to̱kāya̍ ru̱driya̍m ||
translation.text:
1WHAT shall we sing to Rudra, strong, most bounteous, excellently wise, That shall be dearest to his heart?
2That Aditi may grant the grace of Rudra to our folk, our kine, Our cattle and our progeny;
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 29v (OPenn image 31, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.42.1 ‹vi aṃhaḥ vi-mucaḥ napāt›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 30r, begins in RV 1.43.3 ‹yathā naḥ mitraḥ varuṇaḥ›. Verses 1.43.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1kat | rudrāya | pra-cetase | mīḷhuḥ-tamāya | tavyase | vocema | śam-tamam | hṛde
2yathā | naḥ | aditiḥ | karat | paśve | nṛ-bhyaḥ | yathā | gave | yathā | tokāya | rudriyam

translation.original_ref: RV 1.43.3-9 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 3, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 30r
translation.original_text:
3yathā̍ no mi̱tro varu̍ṇo̱ yathā̍ ru̱draś cike̍tati | yathā̱ viśve̍ sa̱joṣa̍saḥ ||
4gā̱thapa̍tim me̱dhapa̍tiṁ ru̱draṁ jalā̍ṣabheṣajam | tac cha̱ṁyoḥ su̱mnam ī̍mahe ||
5yaḥ śu̱kra i̍va̱ sūryo̱ hira̍ṇyam iva̱ roca̍te | śreṣṭho̍ de̱vānā̱ṁ vasu̍ḥ ||
6śaṁ na̍ḥ kara̱ty arva̍te su̱gam me̱ṣāya̍ me̱ṣye̍ | nṛbhyo̱ nāri̍bhyo̱ gave̍ ||
7a̱sme so̍ma̱ śriya̱m adhi̱ ni dhe̍hi śa̱tasya̍ nṛ̱ṇām | mahi̱ śrava̍s tuvinṛ̱mṇam ||
8mā na̍ḥ somapari̱bādho̱ mārā̍tayo juhuranta | ā na̍ indo̱ vāje̍ bhaja ||
9yās te̍ pra̱jā a̱mṛta̍sya̱ para̍smi̱n dhāma̍nn ṛ̱tasya̍ | mū̱rdhā nābhā̍ soma vena ā̱bhūṣa̍ntīḥ soma vedaḥ ||
translation.text:
3That Mitra and that Varuṇa, that Rudra may remember us, Yea, all the Gods with one accord.
4To Rudra Lord of sacrifice, of hymns and balmy medicines, We pray for joy and health and strength.
5He shines in splendour like the Sun, refulgent as bright gold is he, The good, the best among the Gods.
6May he grant health into our steeds, wellbeing to our rams and ewes, To men, to women, and to kine.
7O Soma, set thou upon us the glory of a hundred men, The great renown of mighty chiefs.
8Let not malignities, nor those who trouble Soma, hinder us. Indu, give us a share of strength.
9Soma! head, central point, love these; Soma! know these as serving thee, Children of thee Immortal, at the highest place of holy law.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 30r (OPenn image 31, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.43.3 ‹yathā naḥ mitraḥ varuṇaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 30v, begins in RV 1.44.4 ‹yaviṣṭham atithim su-āhutam juṣṭam›. Verses 1.43.3-9 end on this page.
